rules.text: Kill Seymour, not the mount. Mortiorchis has no death state — its max HP floors at 1,000 and it revives for ever, so every kill is a diminishing tap of HP drained out of Seymour and never a way to remove the adds.
rules.short: Kill Seymour, not the mount

rules.text: Poison him on turn one. 2% of 70,000 is 1,400 a turn, for ever; he never removes it and it does not trigger his HP-threshold reactions.
rules.short: Poison him on turn one — 1,400 a turn, for ever

rules.text: Holy Water a Zombie before the mount acts. Lance of Atrophy sets Zombie, and the mount answers with Full-Life — on a living Zombie that is 100% of max HP as damage plus a guaranteed Death.
rules.short: Holy Water a Zombie before the mount acts

rules.text: Stand the party up before the hit, not after it. Dispel into Cross Cleave arrives with nothing in between, so the only defence is Protect, five Cheer stacks and full HP already being true.
rules.short: Buff before the Dispel, never after it

rules.text: Provoke, the four Breaks and Delay Attack are all dead rows here — both actors are immune, and a delay counters with party-wide Slowga.
rules.short: Provoke, Breaks and Delay are dead rows here

hints.text: {target} is a Zombie and the Mortiorchis answers with Full-Life — cured first it whiffs outright, left alone it is 100% of max HP plus a Death
Poison on turn one is the largest single line in the damage budget: 1,400 a turn off 70,000, for ever, and he never cures it
Haste roughly doubles your turns against theirs — the margin the Holy Water rhythm needs to beat the mount’s Full-Life
Cheer to five: +1 Strength a stack and physical damage received x(15-stacks)/15, a third off every Cross Cleave, and it targets allies so it never provokes a counter
Total Annihilation is magical — Shell halves it, from ~3,300-4,145 to something the party survives
Cross Cleave is ~2,400 on all three against preset HP of 2,420 / 1,500 / 2,310 — unmitigated it is a wipe from full health, and Protect halves it
Mighty Guard is Protect and Shell on the whole party in one turn — Kimahri learned it from Biran Ronso minutes ago, on this mountain
Strip his Reflect and the next Flare detonates on him for ~1,734, then he burns two more turns recasting
Top the whole party up while there is a turn to spare — the Dispel into Cross Cleave pairing cannot be answered, so being full when it lands is the only defence
Stand {target} back up: a downed member is a member the next Cross Cleave cannot be healed through, and KO clears their Haste and Cheer stacks
A summon is a shield before it is a burst — the party leaves the field with frozen counters, his answer is a zero-damage Banish, and the charge ladder stalls while the poison keeps ticking
Heal {target} back over the line: Cross Cleave picks its victim and the only thing that saves them is having been full
Swing at Seymour himself — piercing is the only way past Defense 40, and Auron’s katana and Kimahri’s spear already have it

watch.name: Auto-Attack Mode
watch.advice: Get Shell up — it is ~3,300-4,145 of magic across the party and Shell halves it

watch.name: Ready To Annihilate
watch.advice: Shell now (Defend only halves physical hits, so it will not cut this), and top up anyone who would not survive ~4,300 — a summon stalls the ladder outright

phases.label: Phase 1
phases.note: Lance of Atrophy into Full-Life, then Dispel into Cross Cleave with nothing in between — the physical phase.

phases.label: Phase 2
phases.note: Cross Cleave is gone; it is Flare and the Total Annihilation charge ladder from here, so Shell replaces Protect.

rules.text: Keep one Zombie. Form III opens with Mega Death, and a zombified member is immune to it — cure all three and the active party is wiped from full health.
rules.short: Keep one Zombie alive for Mega Death

rules.text: Never cure the last Zombie while a Mega Death is due. Cure, heal, then let the next Hellbiter re-apply it.
rules.short: Never cure the last Zombie with Mega Death due

rules.text: Dispel her Regen off your Zombies — healing damages a Zombie, so her Regen is a slow execution rather than a gift.
rules.short: Dispel her Regen off your Zombies

rules.text: Form I is a Darkness fight: she counters every landed physical hit with Blind, and Darkness drops physical accuracy to base/10. Cure it or stop swinging.
rules.short: Form I answers every physical hit with Blind

rules.text: Summon only in Form III, and Overdrive on arrival. Aeons postpone Mega Death rather than dying to it, but Mind Blast Curses them on step one and a Cursed aeon can never Overdrive.
rules.short: Summon only in Form III, Overdrive on arrival

hints.text: Cure {target} now — but only because somebody else is still carrying the Zombie that survives Mega Death
Blind is her Form I counter to every landed physical hit, and it takes physical accuracy down to base/10 — the measured run blinded itself out of the fight, 18 hits to 21 misses
Regen on a Zombie is damage, not healing — strip it before it ticks them down
Clear the ailment: Esuna does not touch Zombie, so it can never strip the member who is meant to survive Mega Death
Reflect on the actives nullifies her Form I Blind, Silence and Sleep counters outright, and bounces her Cura and Regen back at her
Haste buys the turns the Holy Water rhythm needs: cure, heal, and still be standing when the next Hellbiter lands
Hold the turn rather than spend it — the supporter is banking a Grand Summon for Form III, where an aeon Overdrive is worth most
Stand {target} up — and single-target only while anyone living is a Zombie, because a revival effect kills a living Zombie outright
Heal {target} clear of the next Hellbiter — she opens Form III on Mega Death and a member at half HP never reaches it
An aeon is a Mega Death delay, not a Mega Death victim — her turn takes the aeon branch and the human step counter freezes where it stands
Spend it now: Mind Blast is step one of her aeon cycle and it Curses, and a Cursed aeon can never Overdrive
Swing — she has no Defense trick, and the fight is decided by whether the party is still standing, not by the damage race

phases.label: Form I
phases.note: She counters every landed physical with Blind and every spell with Silence. Cure the counter or stop swinging; summoning here is a net loss, because Absorb heals her.

phases.label: Form II
phases.note: Hellbiter is party-wide Zombie. Let it land on somebody and leave them zombified — that member is the one who survives the Mega Death that opens Form III.

phases.label: Form III
phases.note: Mega Death opens the form and recurs on her cycle. Only a Zombie survives it. Aeons postpone it and Overdrive on arrival, before Mind Blast Curses them.

rules.text: Talk is a panic button with two charges. It zeroes his Overdrive gauge and costs him his next turn — save both for form 2, where the Overdrive is Ultimate Jecht Shot or a limit-breaking Triumphant Grasp 2.
rules.short: Talk has two charges — spend both in form 2

rules.text: Jecht Beam petrifies at 100%, and the next physical shatters the victim permanently — a shatter is not revivable. Carry a Soft, or a Remedy, and spend it before his next turn.
rules.short: Cure Petrify before the next physical shatters

rules.text: The Yu Pagodas feed his gauge 20% per Power Wave. With both alive he Overdrives about every other turn; killing or slowing them is what makes the two Talk charges enough.
rules.short: Suppress the Pagodas; they feed his Overdrive

rules.text: Aeons are explicitly allowed here — he has a dedicated anti-aeon Overdrive precisely because the designers expected them. Shield cuts Jecht Bomber to a quarter.
rules.short: Aeons are allowed — Shield quarters Jecht Bomber

rules.text: Yu Yevon answers every damaging action with a 9,999 Curaga on himself, so do not hit him. Doom him with a Candle of Life, suppress the Pagodas, and let his own Gravija take 75% of his HP a cast.
rules.short: Never damage Yu Yevon. Doom him instead

hints.text: Spend a Talk: his gauge is nearly full and the Overdrive it buys is party-wide — this resets it to zero and costs him the turn as well
Unpetrify {target} before his next swing — Left-Arm Strike carries shatter chance 100, and a shattered character is gone for good
Triumphant Grasp left {target} zombified, and every heal aimed at a Zombie damages instead
Haste is the whole turn economy here: his Overdrive arrives on his clock, and the party only answers it by getting more turns in between
Slow a Pagoda and its Power Wave stops feeding him 20% a turn — two slowed Pagodas roughly halve how often he Overdrives
Blade Blitz is party-wide and physical, and it becomes his default action below half HP in form 2 — Protect halves every copy of it
Cheer is +1 Strength a stack and physical damage received x(15-stacks)/15, which is exactly the class of damage this fight deals
Bank the HP before the Overdrive, not after — Ultimate Jecht Shot is ~3,300 on everyone and it arrives between the healer’s turns
Stand {target} up: a KO costs the Haste, the Protect and the Cheer stacks as well as the turn
Keep the healer’s MP up — this chain is seven battles long and the party carries its MP across every one of them
Doom kills him in three of his own turns and deals no damage at all, so it never arms the Curaga counter — and the Pagodas’ Power Wave cannot strip it
Idle on purpose: Gravija can never KO anyone (75% of current HP), so with the Pagodas suppressed the party is refusing a race it cannot lose
Keep the Pagodas down, not Yu Yevon — their Power Wave heals him 1,500 a cast, which is more than Gravija takes off him once he is low
Summon freely: Yuna may summon throughout both forms, and Shield cuts the anti-aeon Jecht Bomber to a quarter
Spend the gauge — the possessed aeons mirror your own roster and the chain gives the gauge back between links
Swing at him rather than the Pagodas unless a Pagoda is the one feeding the gauge — form 2 starts at a fresh, full 120,000

phases.label: Jecht
phases.note: Left-Arm Strike by default, Jecht Beam about one turn in four (Petrify at 100%). The Overdrive is Triumphant Grasp: two hits and a Zombie.

phases.label: Jecht, below half
phases.note: Blade Blitz replaces the normal attack outright, so the shatter follow-up now arrives as a party-wide swing, and the Overdrive becomes Ultimate Jecht Shot.

phases.label: Yu Yevon
phases.note: Every damaging action he takes is answered by a 9,999 Curaga on himself. Doom, Zombie and attrition all beat him; damage does not.

phases.label: Possessed Anima
phases.note: Your own aeon, mirrored: the same moveset, the same Overdrive, and the same weaknesses you built it around.

rules.text: Darkness is the damage route. It ignores Defense 160, hits every enemy, costs HP rather than MP, and is free the moment the dressphere is picked up.
rules.short: Darkness is the damage route

rules.text: Magic Break is the strongest opening in the fight. Five casts cap Mega Flare at x0.167 and Impulse at 6.25% of current HP — it defuses the whole win condition.
rules.short: Five Magic Breaks defuse Mega Flare

rules.text: Shell before anything else if there is no Alchemist. Both Impulse and Mega Flare are magic, and Shell is the single action that turns a guaranteed wipe into a guaranteed survival.
rules.short: Shell first when there is no Alchemist

rules.text: Physical attacks are the wrong route: Defense 160 floors them per hit, so Trigger Happy gains nothing from being multi-hit.
rules.short: Physicals are floored by Defense 160

rules.text: The countdown is five dead enemy actions. They are free party turns — bank healing and finish the Break ladder inside them.
rules.short: The countdown is five free party turns

hints.text: Darkness ignores his Defense 160 and hits everything — it is why the Dark Knight dressphere is hidden in this dungeon, immediately before this test
Five Magic Breaks cap every spell he owns at x0.167: Mega Flare 1,152 becomes 192 and Impulse drops to 6.25% of current HP
Mental Break is a flat x1.833 on all your magic and does not care that his Magic Defense is only 10 — it is the follow-up Magic Break has already paid for
Armor Break is x1.833 on physicals — worth having, but it multiplies the weaker route here, and it anti-synergises with Table-turner
Shell halves Impulse and Mega Flare, the two biggest threats in the script, and stacks multiplicatively with Magic Break down to x0.083
Only his turns 2-4 are physical, so Protect is the lesser buff — take it once Shell is up
Heal into the countdown, not out of it — Mega Flare lands on the turn the number reaches zero and it hits everyone
A plain swing is crushed by Defense 160; this is the row to take only when nothing better is charged

watch.advice: Five dead enemy actions, then it lands on everyone — get Shell up, cap Magic Break, and be at full HP on zero

phases.label: The 12-action loop
phases.note: Curse, three physicals, two Impulses, then five countdown turns and Mega Flare. The countdown turns are free; spend them on Breaks and healing.

rules.text: Two Dark Knights on Darkness, one healer. Darkness ignores Defense, reaches the long-range Nodes, and hits every enemy at once — one action clears both Bulwarks or both Redoubts.
rules.short: Two Dark Knights on Darkness, one healer

rules.text: Ignore the Nodes and the Redoubts past the point they stop hurting: the Nodes hold 300,000 HP and the Redoubts revive. All the damage that matters goes into the limb.
rules.short: Ignore the Nodes and Redoubts — hit the limb

rules.text: Against the Tail, raw max HP is the only defence — Tail Beam is a percentage of max HP and Noli Me Tangere is a flat constant, so buffs do nothing.
rules.short: Against the Tail, max HP is the only defence

rules.text: Re-buff after Odi Et Amo. It strips every buff on the party, so Mighty Guard has to go back up before the next cycle.
rules.short: Re-buff after Odi Et Amo strips the party

rules.text: Terror of Zanarkand ignores Defense and hunts one character. Protect still reduces it, armour does not, and one healer stays dedicated to whoever ate it.
rules.short: Terror of Zanarkand: Protect helps, armour does not

hints.text: Darkness ignores Defense, reaches every enemy including the long-range Nodes, and costs HP rather than MP — which Curaga pays for
Shell on all three: Vegnagun’s entire moveset is magic-type, so this is the half that matters most
Protect is the one mitigation Terror of Zanarkand still respects — it ignores Defense, but it is Protect-reducible
A party-wide answer, because the hit that got here was party-wide — Nemo Ante Mortem Beatus fires at every 20% HP milestone the Head crosses
Clear it now: Vita Brevis is party-wide with a guaranteed Delay, and a delayed girl is a girl who is not healing
Keep everyone above the constant — Noli Me Tangere is a flat 1,323 and nothing in the party’s kit reduces it
Stand {target} up before the next cycle — this chain does not stop between links and a downed girl carries into the next one
Magic routes around the Right Redoubt’s Magic Defense 0 while the physicals go at the Left
MP is the chain’s real resource — five battles run on one pool and nothing refills it in between
A free party heal when the MP has run out, which in a five-battle chain it eventually does
Physical damage belongs on the Left Redoubt (Defense 0) — everything else takes magic or Darkness

watch.name: Charge Core
watch.advice: Three unimpeded Core turns and it fires — killing a Bulwark makes the Core waste its turn on Full-Life and stops the counter

watch.name: Memento Mori
watch.advice: It is landing this turn; heal through it and then break the charge by killing a Bulwark

watch.name: Terror of Zanarkand
watch.advice: Nine Defense-ignoring hits on one girl — Protect reduces them, armour does not, and the healer is hers for the next two turns

phases.label: Tail
phases.note: Buffs are near-useless: Tail Beam is a percentage of max HP and Noli Me Tangere a flat constant. Keep everyone above 1,323 HP and hit it.

phases.label: Leg and Nodes
phases.note: All 18,220 HP of damage goes into the Leg; the Nodes hold 300,000 and are not the fight. Green Nodes heal and buff the Leg, which is immune to Reflect.

phases.label: Body and Bulwarks
phases.note: Two Darknesses clear both Bulwarks and chunk the Core. Do not hit a Bulwark twice with the same damage class — they mirror it back.

phases.label: Head and Redoubts
phases.note: Right Redoubt dies to magic, Left to physicals, then burn the Head. Odi Et Amo strips every buff; Nemo Ante Mortem Beatus fires at each 20% milestone.

phases.label: Shuyin
phases.note: Protect and Shell on all three, Haste the attackers, and keep one healer free for whoever Terror of Zanarkand picks.

rules.text: Kill order: Logos, then Ormi, then Leblanc. Either henchman dying switches off No Love Lost, and Ormi only reaches Huggles once he is the last one standing — so Leblanc dies last, not first.
rules.short: Kill order: Logos, then Ormi, then Leblanc

rules.text: Dispel strips Not-So-Mighty Guard in one action — it is Protect, Shell and Regen on all three at once, and Dispel already removes all three statuses.
rules.short: Dispel strips Not-So-Mighty Guard in one action

rules.text: Send magic at Ormi, not swords: his Defense 84 floors physicals but his Magic Defense is only 16, so a Black Mage's Fira does two and a half times what a Warrior's sword does.
rules.short: Magic through Ormi, not swords

rules.text: Bank a heal before Ormi crosses a quarter of his max HP — Concussive Blast hits the whole party for 281-317 and no Defense stat reduces it.
rules.short: Bank a heal before Ormi hits 25% HP

rules.text: Nothing in the bag cures Eject. Russian Roulette rolls exactly one of Death, Petrify, Eject or three lesser statuses, and Logos is the one throwing it — killing him first is the only defence.
rules.short: Nothing cures Eject — kill Logos first

hints.text: Ormi's Magic Defense is only 16 against his Defense 84 — this is the route that actually hurts him
Ignores Defense outright, so it does not care that Ormi's is 84
Strips Protect, Shell and Regen from every Syndicate member at once — the only counter-play the record names for Not-So-Mighty Guard
Dead on Leblanc (she is immune to DEF Down) but works on Logos and Ormi — the same swing, one target it never touches
Dead on Leblanc (STR Down immune) but Ormi and Logos both take it
Top up before Ormi drops under a quarter HP — Concussive Blast is a flat hit to everyone and no armor reduces it
Cures the Petrify Russian Roulette can roll — Eject on the same roll has no cure at all, so keeping Logos' turns down matters more
Logos' Evasion 40 is the highest in the fight — a Warrior misses him over a third of the time; a Gunner or Thief lands close to nine in ten
Her Defense 10 against a Magic Defense of 62 makes the sword the right route on her — the opposite of Ormi

phases.label: ACT I — Chateau Entrance
phases.note: Ormi's Defense 120 floors physicals and his Magic Defense 4 does the opposite — this act exists to teach that split before Act III asks for it under pressure.

phases.label: ACT II — Logos’ Room
phases.note: Logos and Ormi together, the same opposite defensive shapes on the field at once, and Russian Roulette makes its first appearance — Death, Petrify or Eject on a random target.

phases.label: ACT III — the Last Room
phases.note: All three at once. No Love Lost fires on Leblanc's 3rd, 11th and 19th turn while both henchmen are alive — kill either one first and it never triggers again.

rules.text: Steal from each Guardian once. Until you do, every hit on one triggers a 1,000 HP Auto-Potion counter, and they hand Seymour another 1,000 whenever he drops below 4,800 — two turns of Steal removes more healing than most parties can out-damage.
rules.short: Steal from each Guardian — it kills their potions

rules.text: He cycles ice, lightning, water, fire, in that order, and it never varies. His own Scan text says so, which is the point: the matching Nul spell reduces a whole turn to nothing, and it costs 2 MP.
rules.short: Ice, lightning, water, fire — pre-cast the Nul

rules.text: Pain carries a 100% Death rider, so on a party member it is not 500 damage, it is a kill — and on an aeon it is only the 500. That asymmetry is the whole of the middle act: summon, and keep something on the field Anima cannot delete.
rules.short: Pain kills people and only hurts aeons — summon

rules.text: His HP bar is not a progress bar. Emptying it summons his aeon; beating his aeon gives him the whole bar back, stronger. Budget for roughly 27,000 damage, not 6,000.
rules.short: His bar comes back once — budget for 27,000

rules.text: Act one is the only stretch with turns to spare. Haste, Cheer and a stolen potion bought there are still on the board in act three, where two hits a turn land for roughly 1,700 each.
rules.short: Spend act one buying tempo, not damage

hints.text: Take the pouch off {target}: one successful Steal ends its 1,000 HP Auto-Potion counter and its Hi-Potions for Seymour — and nothing else, so it will still Remedy him
His next spell is already decided — the Nul that matches it takes the whole hit to zero, for 2 MP out of a bar of 180
The Guardians have no Petrify resistance at all, and a petrified monster shatters — it forfeits the overkill AP and it ends them in one throw
Poison is 600 a turn on him, a tenth of his bar — but only once the Guardians are dead, because Steal never disabled their Remedy
Break his Magic and act three halves: Banishing Blade lands at a chance that ignores resistance outright and applies all four at once
Tempo bought now is still there in act three, when he takes two turns of damage out of the party for every one of theirs
Oblivion is sixteen hits across everything on the field — unshielded it is a wipe, and shielded an aeon walks out of it
Land it while she is Boosted: she takes half again as much, and the multiplier applies before the damage cap
Shell halves every one of his spells for its whole duration, which is worth more than nullifying one of them once
He opened the fight Shelled and this Yuna has no Dispel — Aerospark is the free aeon sub-command that strips it and doubles every spell aimed at him
One line each from Tidus, Yuna and Wakka, once per battle: +10 Strength and +10 Magic Defense twice, for the whole fight
An aeon is the only body on this field that a 100% Death rider cannot delete, and while it holds the field the party is off-stage with frozen counters
Stand {target} back up — Pain does not damage a party member, it kills them, so this will keep happening until something else is on the field
Top {target} up past the next hit: one of his spells is most of a bar in act one and all of one in act three
While a Guardian stands, a swing aimed at Seymour lands on the Guardian instead — magic is the only thing that reaches him

watch.name: Boost
watch.payload: half again as much damage taken, until her next turn
watch.advice: This is the window — spend the biggest thing the party has before she acts again

watch.payload: Oblivion — sixteen hits across the field
watch.advice: Get Shield up. Her gauge is filling whether she acts or is targeted, and it is a race, not something to eat twice

phases.label: Act 2 - Anima
phases.note: Seymour is on the field and doing nothing. She alternates Boost and Pain while a third clock fills toward Oblivion; an aeon is immune to the kill and only takes the damage.

phases.label: Act 1 - the retinue
phases.note: Two Guardians cover him against anything physical and heal him on a counter. Steal first, end them second, and let the elemental order do the rest.

phases.label: Act 3 - alone
phases.note: Full health again, stronger magic, and the same spell twice in one turn. The published order holds, so the matching Nul still answers it.

rules.text: Cid can move the ship or fire the missiles, never both — pull back the moment the fight opens. FAR is the only range Cid can fire from, and one volley (~2,400) outdamages a whole turn of party swings for no party turn at all.
rules.short: Pull back — Cid does more than you do

rules.text: The Al Bhed Potion is the only heal in this party — no Yuna, no White Magic. Rank 2, party-wide, exactly 1,000, and it cures Poison, Silence and Petrify in the same cast. A petrified member is one Swooping Scythe from being gone for good.
rules.short: Al Bhed Potion is your only heal — use it early

rules.text: When Evrae inhales while the ship is FAR, do nothing that names it. Attacking now makes it Swoop in and breathe anyway — the dodge is refusing the bait, not landing a counter.
rules.short: Ship is FAR and it inhales — do not attack

rules.text: Once its bar drops under a third, everything it does gets worse at once: it goes berserk, and if it is still un-Reflected its next big turn is a self-cast Haste. Reflect denies the Haste and turns it into a free Haste on your own party instead.
rules.short: Under 1/3 HP: get Reflect up before the Haste

rules.text: Slow only helps while it can still be applied — cast it before Reflect goes up, never after, because Slow is reflectable and a Reflected Evrae bounces it onto the party that cast it.
rules.short: Slow before Reflect, never after

hints.text: Cid pulls the ship out of reach — Poison Breath and Swooping Scythe cannot land while it is FAR, and Cid's missiles only fire from out here
Bring the ship NEAR when nothing is charging — Wakka and Lulu can reach at either range, but the rest of the party needs this to swing at all
Stand the party back up to 1,000 and clear Poison, Silence and Petrify in one cast — the only heal this party has without Yuna
Its recovery counter roughly doubles while Slow holds — cast this before Reflect, or a Reflected Evrae bounces it straight back onto {actor}'s own party
Deny the self-Haste it casts under a third HP — Reflected, that same cast lands as a free Haste on {actor}'s own party instead
Blinded, its Attack row goes out — Swooping Scythe still connects, so this only ever blunts half the NEAR-range melee, never all of it
Halves both Attack and Swooping Scythe at once — the one debuff that touches the scythe limbs at all
Stacks up to five and works at FAR — the range game is a setup zone, not a dead one, so bank this while the ship is pulled back
Tempo bought at FAR carries into the NEAR exchanges later — cast it on whoever can already reach from out here
Every element is halved on this thing and holy is neutral — there is no weakness to aim for, only base power, and never into a Reflected Evrae
One of the three swings that reach at FAR, with Lulu's Blk Magic and Wakka's blitzball — and it drains HP and MP on the way
A physical swing rolls to hit like any other — the only thing guaranteed here is Cid missiles and the boss magic, not this
A turn spent on an ally names no enemy. It is the dodge whenever Evrae holds a breath with the ship FAR, because naming Evrae then makes it Swoop in and breathe anyway

watch.name: Inhale
watch.payload: Poison Breath — roughly 1,500 to all three active members at once
watch.advice: If the ship is already FAR, do nothing that names it. If it is NEAR, pull back now — the dodge is a race between two clocks

phases.label: Phase 1 - the range game
phases.note: Pull back, farm the missile volleys, close in only to hit what does not reach from FAR. Stone Gaze's aggro counter builds on every hit landed on it — it resets when Evrae acts, so a quiet turn is never wasted.

phases.label: Phase 2 - do not poke it from FAR
phases.note: Swooping Scythe is live: any attack made at FAR drags the ship back to NEAR on its own. Get Reflect up before its self-Haste lands, and stop re-ordering the ship out — the only order worth a turn from here is the Poison Breath dodge.

rules.text: This is a race. He has 33,000 HP, and every action aimed at him brings Zanmato closer, so each one has to count: spells, a healthy party, and an aeon ready.
rules.short: A race: 33,000 HP before his gauge fills

rules.text: Every action that targets him adds 3 to his gauge, and every attack he makes adds 2. At 100 he uses Zanmato: 9,999 to each member of the party, fatal to all three.
rules.short: Each action aimed at him fills his gauge

rules.text: Defense 80 and Magic Defense 0: a sword lands at about half, a spell at full strength. Lulu is the best attacker in her own fight.
rules.short: Spells, not swords: Lulu hits hardest

rules.text: Once his gauge is high, put an aeon in front of him. Zanmato then hits the aeon, not the party.
rules.short: Gauge high: summon an aeon to take Zanmato

rules.text: Lady Ginnem and Daigoro cannot be targeted. The dog bites only when Yojimbo orders it.
rules.short: Ginnem and Daigoro cannot be targeted

hints.text: Magic Defense 0 takes a -ra spell at full strength, and one cast fills his gauge by one targeting, not one per hit
His gauge is high: an aeon on the field takes Zanmato in place of the party
Keep the party up. A heal names no enemy, so it adds nothing to his gauge
Stand {target} back up. A revive aimed at the party adds nothing to his gauge
Nothing to add this turn. Every action aimed at him fills his gauge, so a quiet turn keeps Zanmato further off
A physical hit lands at about half against Defense 80, and it still fills his gauge

phases.label: The Zanmato gauge
phases.note: Below 25 he only sends the dog. From 25 he adds Kozuka, from 50 Wakizashi, and at 100 Zanmato.

rules.text: Nothing sticks to Trema: every status, every stat change, Gravity and Reflect fail on him. Only damage moves him.
rules.short: No status or Gravity lands on Trema

rules.text: When his HP falls below a half, and again below a quarter, Meteor comes down on the party. Below about a sixth comes Ultima. Heal before you cross each line.
rules.short: Heal before his HP crosses 1/2 and 1/4

rules.text: His spells need MP: drained early, he cannot pay for Demi, Flare or Ultima. One source says this still holds under his Spellspring; it is disputed, so keep the party healed either way.
rules.short: Drain his MP early (one source)

blocks.text: Get ready before the next area, because a boss is waiting there. Buy Holy Water from Wantz: 30 of it, spent at the customize screen, puts Zombie Ward on a piece of armour, and this fight calls for that ward. Equip the armour.
Bring about 30 Phoenix Downs to be safe. Anyone who struggled with the earlier bosses should fill every Overdrive gauge first, since this one is often called the hardest in the game.
Yuna needs Dispel already learned, because it pays off here.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: Seymour's attacks tell you what the Mortiorchis will do. Lance of Atrophy inflicts Zombie, Full-Life follows, and Total Annihilation caps it off.

blocks.text: Seymour again, and this time Kimahri and Yuna can use Trigger Commands: Kimahri's gives +10 Strength and Yuna's gives +10 Magic Defense.
He brings out the Mortiorchis, much like the helper that fought beside him at Bevelle.
Lance of Atrophy can leave one of your party Zombified. Zombie Ward armour (see above) makes that less likely.

Whoever turns Zombie needs a Holy Water, a Remedy or Esuna right away. Full-Life would normally refill a character to full HP, but Zombie flips healing around, so Seymour uses it to KO a Zombie on the spot.
He banishes aeons as he did before, so summon them only as a last resort. Lulu should Bio him early, since the poison piles up a great deal of damage, and Hastega should stay up on the party.
If Seymour puts Reflect or Protect on himself, Yuna should Dispel it so your hits stay worthwhile. Dispel his Reflect quickly enough and he may Flare himself.
Total Annihilation is the dangerous one, and the game announces it. It wipes out a party that is not ready.

Once Seymour is at about half his HP, the Mortiorchis switches to Auto-Attack Mode and then declares that it is Ready to Annihilate. The blast lands on its following turn, and it charges faster after the first one, so keep an eye on those messages all fight.

On the warning, Yuna can cast Shell just before the blast lands, or Kimahri can use the Mighty Guard he learned from Biran, or Rikku can Mix up Mighty G, Super Mighty G, or the top-tier Hyper Mighty G.
Defend will not help against this one: it only halves physical hits, and Total Annihilation is magic. Shell is what halves it.

You can also call an aeon once Ready to Annihilate shows: standing on the field when the blast fires, it takes the whole hit for the party. Do it after Seymour's turn so he cannot Banish it before the attack.
Otherwise, keep up the regular attacks and magic until he drops.
A fight that needs preparing for is ahead. Berserk is off the table now, so take off any armour with Berserk Ward or Berserkproof.
What you will meet instead is Darkness, aimed at characters who attack normally, and Silence, aimed at spellcasters.
Give the fighters (Tidus, Auron, Wakka and Kimahri) Dark Ward or Darkproof armour, and the casters (Yuna and Lulu) Silence Ward or Silenceproof.
Three phases, and a new form for each.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: She heals Zombies with Curaga and Regen, and Holy Water is what cures Zombie. Her counters dispel buffs, and her Mind Blast puts a curse on aeons.

blocks.text: Phase 1 gives her two counters. Hit her physically and the attacker is Blinded; hit her with magic and the caster is Silenced.
Esuna handles both. Items work too: Blind yields to Eye Drops and Silence to Echo Screens, while a Remedy cures either. Rikku's Al Bhed Potions cure Silence and heal in one move.
Now she uses Hellbiter to turn the whole party into Zombies, then casts healing spells that hurt Zombies. Your own healing spells and items hurt them too.
Curing everyone just makes her cast Hellbiter again, so leave at least one character a Zombie at all times. Heal with Holy Water when needed, and let Yuna Dispel any Regen she puts on your party.
Her new spell is Mega Death, which KOs anyone who is not a Zombie. That is one more reason never to cure the last Zombie.
More notes and tactics:
Holy hits her very hard, and Yuna is worth bringing for her Dispel and her healing. If Yuna knows Holy, have her blast away with it for a much easier fight.
Yuna or Rikku can learn Holy at this point, using a Teleport Sphere or Return Sphere together with a Lv. 3 Key Sphere. It sits right along Rikku's usual route on the Sphere Grid.
Reflect on your party bounces the Phase 1 status counters back at her, and her Regen too in Phase 2. If she Regens herself, Dispel it, or she will out-heal you.
Dispelling Slap removes every beneficial status except Reflect, which makes Reflect the dependable one. Put it on Yuna first, and Yunalesca cannot silence her.
Armour that blocks Silence, Darkness and Confuse is good, but think twice about blocking Zombie: you want at least one character to keep it.
Top the party up with potions and ethers if it needs it, and put on any gear that has Stone Ward or Stoneproof. Finish your preparations, then talk to Jecht when you are ready.

blocks.title: Using Powerful Items
blocks.text: The game ends here, so nothing is worth saving: X-Potions, Mega-Potions, Turbo Ethers, Elixirs, Megalixirs and Mega Phoenix are all fair game.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: It feeds on the Yu Pagodas and uses Overdrives whenever its gauge is full. Keep that gauge down: Tidus can Talk to lower it.

blocks.text: The last fight is two battles, one against each form of Braska's Final Aeon. In the second form it draws a sword from its chest and sprouts wings.
Yu Pagodas

Two Yu Pagodas hover on either side of the aeon. Their Power Wave heals it and fills its Overdrive gauge, which is the black bar beside the boss. Destroying them is possible, but they come back a few turns later with extra HP.
Each starts at 5,000 HP and returns with that plus your overkill. Knock one down with a 3,000 hit and then another 3,000 and it comes back with 6,000.
Big hits are therefore a problem. Take both Pagodas down together: if only one falls, the other starts casting nasty spells, Curse included. Better still, leave them alone until the second phase.
Use every helpful status you have; Hastega, Protect and Regen are all a big help.

A petrified character needs a Soft or a Remedy at once. The aeon will Shatter a petrified character and remove them from the fight for good, and finishing the boss with two characters is extremely hard.
Tidus's Talk, one of the Trigger Commands, drains the aeon's Overdrive gauge. Hold it for the second form, when the sword appears, because its Overdrives hit far harder from then on.
Talk can empty the gauge completely, and you get two uses of it over the whole fight.
Bio can poison it, though it may take a few casts to stick. The Break attacks (Armor Break, Power Break, Mental Break, or Full Break for all of them) also help bring its HP down faster.
A final fight against Yu Yevon follows, and it cannot be lost. If it drags, have Yuna cast Reflect on him. Then sit back and watch the ending cinematic!
Dark Knight is among the strongest dresspheres in the game, with a slow but heavy attack and strong defense. Put one of your girls in it now.
Save, and start one girl as a Thief so she can steal from the bosses ahead. A Ribbon on one party member is also worth having, to block nasty status effects.
Time to take on an aeon! Remember to Steal a Mute Shock off him before the battle ends.
Bahamut cycles through one fixed attack pattern:

items: “Curse” or an ordinary physical hit (Curse locks a girl into her current dressphere)

blocks.text: Then the cycle starts over. The first Impulse tells you Countdown is near, and Mega Flare hurts badly, so have everyone fully healed before it comes.
Impulse cannot kill: it takes a percentage of HP, like Demi.
With a pattern this simple there is little more to say. If you are struggling, grind some EXP by the Save Sphere to level up your Dark Knights.
Climbing Vegnagun is easy; you barely need a map to reach each fight in order. The Tail comes first and needs no preparation.
As said above, there is not much to prepare, and little strategy is needed. The Tail serves as a gateway and a check on your gear and levels for the battles ahead.
If its attacks are too much for you to survive, reload an earlier save and level up a little first.
It has just two attacks:

items: “Tail Beam,” its ordinary attack, takes 31.25% of the target’s maximum HP
“Noli Me Tangere” does 1,250 damage to everyone

blocks.text: The Tail idles on its first turn, then opens with Noli Me Tangere and uses it once more below 25% HP. Survive those two and the fight is easy.
Dark Knight dresspheres help: many Tail attacks take a percentage of HP, but a bigger HP pool gives whoever heals (White Mage or Alchemist) longer to respond.
Dark Knights also hit hard with ordinary attacks and with Darkness.
Carry on up the path toward Vegnagun. Before the top, protect the party against Berserk with accessories such as Ribbons.
Elemental affinity accessories (Tetra Guard, Tetra Bracelet, Tetra Band) also cut incoming damage. Ahead, the Leblanc Syndicate is already fighting Vegnagun’s Leg and its “nodes”.
Four targets here: the Leg, your main target, and three Nodes high up on the body. The Leg’s attacks:

items: “Vita Brevis”: damage to every party member and a long delay on their next turns
“Absorb”: steals HP and MP from a target

blocks.text: Now the Nodes (A, B and C). What a Node does depends on its colour, and it cycles through three colours in order as it acts or gets hit:
Red:

items: “Dies Irae” strikes all three girls at random, up to 9 hits

blocks.text: Green:

items: Cura, Regen, Shell or Protect on the Leg

blocks.text: Yellow:

items: Firaga, Blizzaga, Thundaga or Waterga on all targets
Flare, aimed at a single target

blocks.text: Hitting the Nodes will not switch them off; it only changes their colour, and none is a good one for you: they either damage the party or heal the Leg. Put your effort into taking the Leg down fast.
Protect and Shell on the party reduce damage, and a Dispel Tonic on the Leg clears the buffs a Green Node gives it.
The Nodes have far too much HP to kill. This is a war of attrition: can you out-damage the Leg before four enemies’ damage overwhelms you?
Keep climbing toward Ormi and Logos. Before the next fight, guard against Petrification and Poison. Past them you join Nooj, Gippal and Leblanc, who are already fighting Vegnagun’s Core.
Jecht’s voice explains the mechanic soon after the fight starts. The Bulwarks react to an attack on the Core depending on how it was made. Their replies:

head: Your Attack Type
Bulwark Response
rows: Damage worth 31.25% of a character’s maximum HP
A drain of 18.75% of a character’s maximum MP
Both at once: 18.75% of maximum HP in damage, plus 18.75% of maximum MP drained

blocks.text: Core:

items: “Charge Core”: three charges must pass before “Memento Mori” becomes available
“Memento Mori”: heavy magic damage to the whole party
Full Life, used whenever a Bulwark has been KO’d

blocks.text: Bulwark Retaliation Attacks:
Those are the Bulwarks’ answers to attacks. They also act on their own turns:
The Left Bulwark casts harmful spells at your party:
The Right Bulwark buffs itself and its two allies, the Left Bulwark and the Core:

The easiest way to beat the Core is to take out both Bulwarks first and keep them down most of the fight. They have only 3,000 HP each, and multi-target attacks such as a Dark Knight’s Darkness make it easier.
Protect or Shell on the party is pointless, since the Left Bulwark’s Dispel strips them, but a Warrior’s Armor Break on the Core raises the damage it takes over the fight.
Memento Mori is the toughest attack. Ideally it never gets used.
If it does, switch to a White Mage and have her quickly cast Shell on the party, to improve your odds against the heavy magic damage (assuming it is not dispelled first).
A hidden timer runs this fight: once Shuyin has spoken seven times, the cannon goes off and the fight ends in a Game Over.
There is plenty of time even for low-level characters, so the timer rarely matters.
Here is what each of the three targets can do:
Head:

items: “Pallida Mors”: magic damage of roughly 1,200 on one target, used only while the Head is untargetable
“Nemo Ante Mortem Beatus”: roughly 1,490 to 1,685 magic damage
“Mors Certa”: 250 magic damage plus Silence, Darkness and Poison
“Odi Et Amo”: 16 hits spread across the party, about 1,000 in all, and it can strip buffs such as Shell, Protect, Reflect, Regen, Haste and stat boosts
“Acta Est Fabula”: revives both Redoubts at full HP

blocks.text: Right Redoubt:

items: “Lacrimosa”: a physical hit of about 100 on one target

blocks.text: Left Redoubt:

items: “Dispel”: strips the target of its buffs
“Demi”: hits each target for 25% of its current HP

blocks.text: Two phases. In the first, the Head cannot be attacked until both Redoubts are down (do not let one revive the other).
The second phase starts when you first KO both: the Head uses Acta Est Fabula to bring them back, and from then on it can be targeted.

In phase two, use attacks that hit every target, like a Dark Knight’s Darkness, since it pierces physical and magic defense alike. If you KO a Redoubt, the Head spends its turns reviving it instead of attacking.

The Head/Shuyin uses Nemo Ante Mortem Beatus, its strongest attack, four times, at 80%, 60%, 40% and 20% HP. Each cast hits for roughly 1,490 to 1,685, so be ready to recover by keeping everyone above 1,685 HP, and keep a White Mage or Alchemist on hand.
The last fight of the game is more spectacle than strategy. His attacks look great and hit hard, and the job is to ride out the big ones while whittling his HP.
His moves, many of them lifted from Tidus’s attacks in Final Fantasy X:
It is worth watching every one of them before you finish the fight.
Go into the Hidden Passageway. Ormi and some Syndicate members soon ambush you, but they are extremely easy to beat. Follow the passage to the Save Sphere and save.
A second ambush, by Logos and Ormi, comes later, and they are extremely easy again; they seem not to have levelled while Yuna, Rikku and Paine earned all that EXP.
The last fight is against Leblanc, Ormi and Logos. Like the Syndicate fights before it, it needs no elaborate strategy and is very easy.

blocks.title: Charm Bangle
blocks.text: It is easy to miss because it is a one-time fight, but Logos drops a very useful item: the Charm Bangle, which gives No Encounters and stops random battles.
Using it this early is generally not advised, since your characters need the EXP, but now you have it in your toolkit.
When the fight ends, the mission is over and Leblanc teams her Syndicate up with the Gullwings, who share a goal. You receive the Reassembled Sphere key item.
Save your game and shop at O'aka's before the temple fight, because a boss is next.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: His spells run ice, lightning, water, fire in a fixed order, so Yuna should Nul each in turn: NulFrost, NulShock, NulTide, NulBlaze. Cornered, he summons.

blocks.text: You face Maester Seymour and two Guado Guardians. The Guardians put Protect on themselves, and Seymour puts Shell on himself.
Tidus, Yuna and Wakka all have Trigger Commands here: Tidus's Talk raises Seymour's Strength, while Yuna's and Wakka's raise their own Magic Defense.

A physical attack on Seymour makes a Guardian step in front of him. The Guardians are hard to kill because of Auto-Potion: they heal themselves with a potion every time they are hit. There are two ways around it:

items: Rikku Steals from each Guardian, which leaves them without Hi-Potions.
Auron's Threaten stuns them, so they cannot act.

blocks.text: Kill both Guardians before turning to Seymour, and have Yuna cast the matching Nul spell (NulBlaze, NulShock, NulTide or NulFrost) ahead of each of his spells.
The rest of this battle is covered below.
Tidus opens by suggesting that Yuna summon her new aeon, listed only as question marks. It is Shiva.
Blizzara heals Shiva fully at any time: ice is her own element and she absorbs it, so the spell restores her HP rather than hurting her.
Keep healing her until Diamond Dust, her Overdrive, is ready, fire it at Anima, and repeat until Anima falls.
Diamond Dust does extra damage if you fire it while Anima is boosting.

Shiva will probably be KO'd along the way, so back her up with regular attacks on Anima and keep party HP as high as you can. Anima's Overdrive is close to a guaranteed wipe, and her Pain move is an instant KO on one party member.
After Anima falls, Auron can use Magic Break on Seymour, and Lulu can poison him with Bio if she has it.
Most players find Evrae one of the most troublesome bosses in the game. Your levels and style matter, but it is worth preparing well regardless.
Wear Stoneproof or Stone Ward armour and Poisonproof or Poison Ward armour if you have any. A proof ability removes the chance of that status entirely; a Ward only lowers it, so it can still land.
You can add these wards to armour you own: 30 Softs from Rin give Stone Ward in an open slot, 30 Antidotes give Poison Ward, and armour with two open slots can take both.
Make sure Wakka and Rikku are properly equipped, because they will carry this fight. Lulu is an option too if she is among your higher-level characters.
In the final room (the one with the Save Sphere), talk to the Al Bhed standing on the left for four Al Bhed Potions, then go through the gates at the back to start.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: High Magic Defense and no elemental weakness. Repeated melee hits make it exhale Poison Breath. Have Cid move the ship away and he fires Guided Missiles.

blocks.text: How the fight works:
Evrae is a flying wyrm, and the fight takes place outside the Fahrenheit as you approach Bevelle. Cid takes your orders: on his turn the ship either moves closer to Evrae or pulls farther away.
Up close, Evrae can use Stone Gaze, which may petrify, and Poison Breath, which may poison. That is why the armour above matters.
While the ship is far off, Cid fires Guided Missiles (Salvos) on his own, at most 3 times in total.
The strategy:
Begin by pulling the ship away. Tidus uses Cheer to raise the team's Strength and Defense; it stacks up to 5 times, and there is plenty of time for that while the ship is distant.
Wakka keeps attacking all fight long, because his shots reach Evrae from any distance.
From far away Evrae hits weakly, so retreat whenever you need to catch your breath. It also gives Cid time for his Guided Missiles, which hurt a lot.
Rikku's Use command with Al Bhed Potions heals the team and clears Poison and Petrify. Her Overdrive, Mix, can also produce Mighty G or Super Mighty G.
Mighty G puts Protect and Shell on everyone, cutting all of Evrae's damage; Super Mighty G also grants Haste and Regen.
Rikku is the best healer here, so field Wakka, Rikku and Tidus, and swap Lulu in for Tidus if you want more damage.
Tidus can Slow or Slowga Evrae to get more turns. At 1/3 HP, though, Evrae starts casting Haste on itself, which cancels any Slow, and it casts Haste again at once if you re-Slow it.
Cheer makes Wakka's ordinary attacks hit Evrae very hard. Keep at it until it goes down.
The Cavern of the Stolen Fayth can be done on your initial trip through the Calm Lands, but it is best to return when your characters are far stronger. The game is easy to finish without Yojimbo.

blocks.title: Kimahri's Overdrive - Ronso Rage
blocks.text: Use Lancet on a Ghost in this area and Kimahri can learn the Doom Ronso Rage.
In the next area an unsent summoner, Lady Ginnem, waits. Lulu once guarded her. She starts the fight and calls up Yojimbo.
Yojimbo is not too hard to beat, and Yuna's aeons are there if you struggle. He has 33,000 HP.
This is the lowest floor of the Via Infinito. Two bosses wait here: Paragon first, then Trema straight after with no break in between.

blocks.title: Paragon Oversoul
blocks.text: Trigger Paragon in its Oversouled form, which is recommended. If you have worked through the bestiary you may already have done so; otherwise it is not hard.
Paragon belongs to the Weapon family with Ultima Weapon and Omega Weapon. Defeat ten of them in total, then flee from the next one when it triggers an Oversoul.
Ultima Weapons turn up on floors 47 to 49 and Omega Weapons on floors 75 to 79.
To prepare, level your characters well, have their best dresspheres (Mascot above all), and carry strong accessories (Invincible, Crystal Bangle, Rabite’s Foot, Shining Bracer, Defense Bracer).
Equipping the Higher Power Garment Grid is also recommended: it gives Break HP Limit, and pushing through each of its gates adds the Break Damage Limit Auto-Ability.
As noted above, face Paragon in its Oversoul form, which is actually easier. Until it falls under 40% HP it leaves you alone unless you provoke it.
That leaves time to recover between hits, heal damage, and get Break Damage Limit going from the very first turn.
In its normal form it uses:

items: An ordinary attack (can inflict Poison, Itchy, Confusion, Ignore Defense or Absorb HP)
“Genesis”: cone-shaped magic damage that strips helpful statuses such as Auto-Life, Protect, Shell, Reflect, Regen and Haste
“Big Bang”: up to 25,000 damage, used only as a counter to special attacks that bypass Protect and Shell

blocks.text: In its Oversoul form it uses:

items: An ordinary attack with no status effects
Demi, in reply to any healing ability you use
“Judgement”: magic damage to one party member
“Genesis” and “Big Bang” if 20 seconds pass without an attack from you (same effects as above)

blocks.text: The main point is to leave this fight ready for the harder battle with Trema. Using the Higher Power grid, cycle every girl through the dresspheres.
Avoid magic, MP Absorb, Supernova and every Arcana except Black Sky: Paragon fires them straight back at whoever used them.
You will probably just have to grind through it. A party of two Dark Knights and an Alchemist remains viable, as does one of three Mascots.
You can also use the idle time at the start to drink Stamina Tonics, which lift HP for the remainder of the battle, and to put up status buffs.
A short cutscene follows Paragon’s defeat and leads straight into the next fight. Your party starts it in the condition it ended this one, so mind low HP or MP.
Trema has two hard things going for him: heavy damage output and a ridiculous HP pool, 999,999. It is a long fight however strong your attacks are.
His attacks include:

items: “Dying Star”: three physical hits on one target
“Falling Leaf”: three weak physical hits on one target, right after Dying Star
“Thundering Wave”: three physical hits on one target, right after Falling Leaf

blocks.text: He picks at random, except that Falling Leaf and Thundering Wave always follow a Dying Star. He also casts Meteor at 50% HP and again at 25%, and Ultima once he is under 16%.
It is nothing but an onslaught of damage, with no surprises and nothing complicated about the pattern.
Have one girl heal the others all the time, use Stamina Tonic to keep everyone’s HP extra high, and use buffs such as Protect and Shell to cut damage.
Mostly it is a level and gear check, with a bit of luck involved. If you are struggling, keep levelling your characters.
Three aeons wait on the same three platforms whichever route you took down, and you only fight them once. Consider protecting the party against Stop, for example with a Ribbon.
Shiva is the easiest of the three aeons on the Road to the Farplane. Her attacks:

items: Triple attack on three random targets, about 400 HP each
“Heavenly Strike”: cuts one target’s current HP and MP to half, with a 30% chance of Stop

blocks.text: Diamond Dust gets more frequent the faster her HP falls, but unless everyone is Stopped at once you should survive what she dishes out.
She absorbs ice and is weak to fire.
The three sisters dodge many physical attacks, so they can be harder than Shiva, but their moves are simple:
Sandy:
Mindy:

items: “Passado”: 15 hits, each 6.25% of current HP (it cannot kill)
One of Firaga, Blizzaga, Thundaga or Waterga

blocks.text: Cindy:

items: “Absorb”: drains a target’s HP and MP
“Not-So-Mighty Guard”: Shell, Protect and Regen on all three sisters
“White Highwind”: heals the sisters completely, but only while all three live and each is under a quarter HP
“Delta Attack”: drops your whole party to 1 HP, usable only while all three sisters live

blocks.text: Delta Attack, their strongest, needs all three alive, so a quick kill stops it. Mindy is the weakest, but Cindy has the most irritating abilities, so take her down first.
White Highwind also needs all three alive, so the worst plan is spreading damage evenly. Concentrate on one sister at a time.
Sandy and Mindy have high evasion and are hard to hit physically. Specials such as a Lady Luck’s Four Dice or a Dark Knight’s Darkness get past it.
If you are really stuck, a Samurai’s Spare Change can throw 75,000 Gil at one sister for 9,999 damage and nearly kill her outright.
They carry good items to steal: Chaos Shock, White Cape and Potpourri are all worth taking before the fight ends.
This fight lacks the flood of attacks the Sisters throw at you, and you will not have trouble hitting such a huge aeon. But Anima is strong, and uses:

items: A normal attack for about 300 damage that also Poisons
“Pain”: about 300 damage to one target, plus Silence, Itchy and Poison, and it lowers stats

blocks.text: Each Pain lowers the target’s stats further, so have a Remedy ready for anyone it hits more than once. Keep the party healed and you will be fine.

blocks.title: Gun Mage Blue Bullet
blocks.text: Bosses here can teach Gun Mages the Blue Bullet abilities Mortar and Drill Shot. This is the only place in the story to learn Mortar, and your last chance at Drill Shot if you have not learned it yet.
Preparation:
Make sure the whole party is fully healed before starting. There is a lot of good loot to Steal or Mug from these bosses, so keep a Thief dressphere or the Treasure Hunt grid handy.
Also consider setting up one girl on the Salvation Promised grid, assuming you own it.

Baralai is tougher than Rikku or Paine, but they are back in your party to balance things. If you want every Blue Bullet, this is the fight where your Gun Mage should learn Drill Shot. His full move list:

items: Ordinary physical attack: up to three hits of about 300 each
“Glint”: can strike several targets standing close together (you cannot control that)
“Looming Glacier”: Stop, and every target’s MP falls to zero
“Drill Shot”: fires automatically once Baralai’s HP has changed 8 times, at whoever made the last change
Silence on the whole party, and Regen on himself
“Not-So-Mighty Guard”: Shell, Protect and Regen on himself
“Absorb”: takes HP and MP from one target

blocks.text: He has many high-damage attacks that hit several girls, and he drains your MP all fight long.
To steer Drill Shot onto the right girl, have the right Gun Mage keep attacking him until he fires it, ideally without hitting hard enough to end the fight early.
As in earlier fights, remember to Steal or Mug his Nature’s Lore accessory.
The key task here is getting your Gun Mages to learn Mortar from Gippal if you plan on teaching them Blue Bullets. It is their only chance, and he does not use Mortar until he is below 33% HP.
Besides Mortar, which hits a cone in front of him, he also uses:

items: “Bullseye”: removes 56.25% of every target’s remaining HP and can strike several girls
“Flash Bomb”: light damage, may inflict Darkness
“Hush Grenade”: light damage, may inflict Silence

blocks.text: Be ready to heal right after Bullseye, since it is easy for him to KO someone left low. You cannot dodge much of this either, because Grinder and Mortar ignore defense stats.
Many of his attacks sweep an arc in front of him. You cannot position your girls, but you can spread them by moving a couple into ranged roles such as Gun Mage or Gunner.
Heal up before the final blow, and be sure to steal his White Lore accessory.
This is the trickiest fight of all, though at least you need not bother teaching any Blue Bullets here. His attacks:

items: Normal attack: a single shot for about 500
“Rippling Chroma”: about 1,500 magic damage to one target, ignoring magic defense
“Greedy Aura”: takes 18.75% of every girl’s maximum HP and maximum MP
“Lightfall”: 5,000 damage to everyone, used once only, after his HP drops below 3,000

blocks.text: He hits hard, and Lightfall is tough to survive without some preparation. Here is how to get ready.

Best: put one girl in the Dark Knight dressphere for tougher defenses and keep Protect and Shell on her against all other damage. That does not reduce Lightfall, but it keeps her HP high enough to survive it.

Another way: let one girl work through the Salvation Promised Garment Grid for Auto-Life, which revives her after Lightfall. Mix can also help: a Dark Matter together with any potion gives brief party-wide immunity.
With luck you may bring him from 3,000 HP straight to zero.
Remember to Steal or Mug his Arcane Lore before the fight ends.
Completing the Den of Woe gives you the Magical Dances, Vol. I key item, besides each boss’s drops (Crystal Ball and Kaiser Knuckles).
Your next boss fight is upstairs. Despite how it looks, only one of its attacks is lightning damage, which makes a Yellow Ring or NulShock Ring less useful than it sounds.
Be sure to Steal or Mug Ixion’s Sprint Shoes before the fight ends.
Ixion follows a clear pattern. It casts Aerospark, which takes 62.5% of a girl’s current HP; it then recharges, healing some of its HP; then it casts Thor’s Hammer.
Thor’s Hammer hurts your party quite a bit (about 700), so have everyone healed before it lands.
Ixion absorbs lightning damage but is weak to water: Water, Watera, Waterga, Liquid Steel, or Water Gems made with Mix.
Ixion, unlike Yojimbo, can be hit by Warrior Break abilities, which are useful if the fight drags on.
This fight is all magic, so put every character in any armour that guards against magic. That covers:

items: Fire Ward, Lightning Ward, Water Ward and Ice Ward
SOS NulBlaze, SOS NulShock, SOS NulTide and SOS NulFrost

blocks.text: Strip off weapons with Firestrike, Lightningstrike, Waterstrike or Icestrike: hitting him with one could heal him.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: The four Mortiphasms behind him energise his spells, and where they point shapes his actions. Physical hits turn them left, magic turns them right.

blocks.text: The discs hovering behind Omnis are the Mortiphasms. They turn as the fight goes on, and the colours nearest Seymour set the strength and element of his spells.
Fire shows as orange or red, Lightning as yellow or green, Water as blue and Ice as purple.
Seymour casts four spells a turn. If all four discs match, he casts the top-tier spell (Firaga, Thundaga, Waterga or Blizzaga) and absorbs that element when you cast it at him.

He is also weak to the opposite element then. With three matching discs he still absorbs that element but is no longer weak to the opposite one; with two matching discs he is immune to it, and with one he resists it.
Scan shows his elemental strengths and weaknesses.
After six attacks on him, Seymour glows red, starts casting Dispel, and uses Ultima on the party. The glow ends once Ultima has been cast.
This Ultima is much weaker than the Sphere Grid one but still does serious damage, roughly 4,000 HP per character. Heal before he casts it.
Shield can help you survive it, and Lulu's Focus raises your resistance to it as well.
Aeons work well here, which is rare against Seymour, because he does not banish them. Yuna's Nul spells also reduce the damage.
Open with Hastega, Armor Break and Mental Break, and recast whatever Seymour dispels.
Hitting the Mortiphasms turns them and makes his strongest spells less likely. Some sit in the back row, so use Wakka or Lulu to reach them.
Save and restock from O'aka, then run along the walkway to begin the fight with Maester Seymour. A second Save Sphere waits at the far end of the Highbridge.
Fighting Seymour Natus gets far easier if Yuna has Reflect, so level her on the Highbridge against random fiends until she learns it.
Wear any armour with Stone Ward or Stoneproof, and check that Lulu already has Bio.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: Still elemental, but now in multi-casts. Weakened, he petrifies with Break and then uses the non-elemental Flare.

blocks.text: Seymour Natus has two parts you can target, Natus and Mortibody. Natus is Seymour himself; Mortibody is the small alien arm on his left. The fight has three phases, each with its own pattern.

Mortibody casts Desperado throughout, which strips helpful statuses (Haste, Protect, Shell, Reflect) from the party. It happens automatically when three of your party share one status, so spread statuses carefully.
Phase 1
In Phase 1 Mortibody only casts basic spells, cycling through the elements. Natus follows soon after with a Multi-cast double of the same element.
Yuna's Nul spells (NulBlaze, NulShock, NulTide, NulFrost) could block that damage if cast between the two attacks, but fitting her turn there is tricky, even if it can be done.
Just keep attacking until the phase ends, once you have dealt 24,000 damage.
Phase 2 (when Natus drops under 24,000 HP)
Natus starts the phase by putting Protect on himself, which Dispel removes if you have it. He also begins casting Break on single characters, which petrifies them.
Mortibody's Shattering Claw destroys a petrified character it hits, removing them for good, so use a Soft or Yuna's Esuna on Petrify immediately.
Phase 3 (when Natus drops under 12,000 HP)
Now Seymour casts Flare at party members for about 2,500 HP apiece, and Mortibody starts casting Cura on Natus, which makes the last 12,000 HP a slog.
Reflect on Natus sends those Cura spells onto one of your party instead, which makes the fight far easier.
Some additional notes:
Attacking Mortibody is an option. Each time you kill it, Mortibsorption takes 4,000 HP from Natus and revives it; the amount then drops to 3,000, then 2,000, and finally stays at 1,000.
Taking Natus down in 1,000-HP slices still beats dealing with his Flare. If your characters have Reflect, attack Natus directly instead.

items: Summoning an aeon does little, since Natus uses Banish at once. Yuna's Grand Summon can still give you a quick aeon Overdrive.
Yuna’s Talk, one of the Trigger Commands, raises her Magic Defense when used on Seymour, which helps a lot; Tidus and Auron can Talk to him too, for a Strength boost.

blocks.text: Strategy:

items: Reflect on Yuna makes this fight much easier. If you have trouble, level her on the Highbridge until she learns it, and put Reflect on every character for the last phase.

Haste only two party members: Mortibody uses Desperado, which removes all positive statuses, whenever all three are Hasted. Do this before putting Reflect on the party, or the Haste will reflect onto Natus.
Have Lulu cast Bio on Seymour very early. The fight is slow, so the poison has time to add up.
Without Reflect, Shell should go on just two of the party, cast by Yuna.
Put Reflect (or Shell, if you lack it) on Natus himself so that Mortibody cannot heal him much with Cura.
Advanced: make sure every character lands at least one attack on Mortibody or Natus, so all of them earn AP.

blocks.text: The next couple of battles are Yuna's alone. If you have not used her much, charge her Overdrive to full before walking down the hallway.
At the end of the red-lit hallway a short cutscene begins: Yevon has ordered Isaaru to stop you, so he fights Yuna with his aeons.
Isaaru opens by summoning Grothia, essentially Ifrit under a new name.
If you charged Yuna's Grand Summon, use it to bring out Bahamut, then fire his Mega Flare Overdrive for big damage fast.
Mega Flare might not finish Grothia, and then Grothia hits Bahamut with its Hellfire Overdrive.
Bahamut is probably hurt by now. If he came through well and has another Overdrive charged, use it on Valefor.
Otherwise summon Ixion and heal him with his own Thundara when he needs it: aeons absorb their own element, so lightning restores Ixion instead of hurting him.
Pterya has 12,000 HP, so you need a bit more firepower to take it down.
Isaaru's final aeon is Spathi, a Bahamut clone, so you cannot summon Bahamut this time. Summon Shiva instead.
Shiva suits this fight: she is fast, and she is your second-strongest aeon after Bahamut.
Spathi counts down from 5 to 1 and then casts Mega Flare. Shiva's Shield, used just before, is the one way to survive it.
Afterwards heal Shiva with Blizzara; Spathi starts another count right away.
Spathi resists the slow from Heavenly Strike, and you want your MP for Blizzara, so use plain attacks to wear Spathi down.
Beat Spathi and the fight with Isaaru is over.
The next fights are against Sin itself. Its armour is very high, so make sure Auron (or someone else) has learned Armor Break. Levelling is easy: go back to the Zanarkand Ruins and fight fiends.
The Left Fin and the Right Fin are the same fight, and you do it twice in a row.
This fight plays much like Evrae outside the airship. Order Cid, through the Trigger Commands, to pull the ship farther from Sin and the Fin attacks less often.
The ship starts far away, so you must use Move In before you can attack.
Before you close in, spend the spare time powering up with Tidus's Cheer, Rikku's Luck and similar abilities, which stack for up to five uses each.
Cast Hastega early, but remember that Sin's Negation wipes every positive status from your party, so you will have to recast them.
Sin's armour is fairly high, so Auron's Armor Break can speed things up. Negation also removes the Armor Break from Sin, so apply it again if that happens.
When “Core Gathers Energy” appears, act at once with the Trigger Commands and get the ship out of range. Gravija follows shortly and takes about 3/4 of everyone's HP.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: Once the core is energised it casts Gravija, cutting everyone's HP by 3/4, so have Cid back off. It uses Negation, and sometimes a physical attack on everyone.

blocks.text: It plays by the same rules as the last fight.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: Once its HP is halved it withdraws into its shell the turn after, heals itself with Cura if struck there, and comes out a turn later. Inside the shell Gravija cannot touch it.

blocks.text: Begin by killing Sinspawn Genais, which sits in front of Sin's core and absorbs any magic aimed straight at Sin. Unlike the Geneaux at Kilika Temple, this one starts out of its shell.
Genais is weak to Fire. Below 50% HP it withdraws into its shell and starts healing itself with Cura. It has about 20,000 HP, so just keep hitting it until it falls.
Slow, or Silence Buster, limits how often it can cast Cura.
Sin (Core)
This is just like the Left and Right Fin fights, except that you cannot dodge Gravija by moving the ship, and Sin answers regular attacks with low-level spells.
It may Poison your party. Cure that with Rikku's Al Bhed Potion, Yuna's Esuna, or an Antidote or Remedy from anyone.

blocks.label: In Game Description
blocks.value: It drags the airship in while it gathers its power for the ultimate terror, Giga-Graviton. Stop it before it wipes everyone out!

blocks.text: This battle runs on a clock: after about thirteen turns Sin uses its Overdrive, Giga-Graviton, an attack that ends the game on the spot.
The bar above its head shows how near it is to firing. Summoning an aeon will not save you, so you must deal all 140,000 damage before then.
Sin begins too far away to hit and slowly drifts into melee range. Spend the early turns buffing with Cheer, Luck and the like, and Tidus should put Hastega on everyone.
Lulu or Wakka in the party can do damage even while Sin is distant.
Auron should use Armor Break as soon as Sin is close enough. Rikku can get the same Armor Break by Mixing a pair of items (two Power Spheres, say, or two Ability Spheres) into a Frag Grenade.
Once Sin is close to the ship it starts attacking, so be ready for Petrify, Confuse and Zombie.
